title: Who Wrote the Rules
concept: The University of Alaska regents have a first systemwide AI plan, AI Engaged, before them, and two UAA professors write in an op-ed that Anthropic's Claude produced the first draft and that this wasn't disclosed until October 9th, while five faculty answer that the use was not concealed. Both sides agree AI was used and disagree only about whether anyone hid it. At UAA 119 of 150 students cited for misconduct used AI, about 1.1 percent of more than 10,500 students and cited cases only. No decision on the plan had been reported. The film proposes one plain disclosure line on the plan, the same rule the plan sets for AI (it recommends, a person decides), and discloses that its own pipeline is built on Claude. A mint rubber-stamp robot named StampBot is the hero and a gold question token the throughline, ending as DISCLOSED on a footnote strip.

fingerprint.palette: saturated tangerine office walls, deep teal desks, cream legal pads, a mint clerk robot with an oxblood arm and raspberry ink
fingerprint.metaphor: a rubber stamp that has rejected student essays all semester is asked to stamp the university's own AI plan and finds a blank footnote strip where the disclosure should be

palette: saturated tangerine office walls, deep teal desks, cream legal pads, a mint clerk robot with an oxblood arm and raspberry ink
divergence_note: The last five films were a night cab (11-02), an overcast moss slope (11-01), a sage-and-cream chart desk (10-31), an aubergine dusk depot (10-29) and a green-black sonar abyss (10-28). This film is a saturated tangerine daylight office with deep teal desks, cream paper and a mint rubber-stamp hero, lit by hard noon window light. It has no cab, slope, depot or sea cutaway, and its signature object is a gold question token that changes its engraving at every act boundary and lands as DISCLOSED on a footnote strip that sat blank from the first shot.

treatment.title: The Footnote
treatment.summary: Comedian has the best recurring gag (missing footnote strip), the fairest Test, 5 gags, shelf-only. Explainer's dot field supplies the scale reveal. Dramatist's concession keeps the rebuttal unmocked.

angle.thesis: Both sides agree AI helped draft the University of Alaska's AI Engaged plan and disagree only about whether anyone could tell, so the cheap fix is one plain disclosure line on a public document, the same rule the plan asks of AI: it recommends, a person decides.
supporting_facts: c20 both sides agree AI was used, they dispute whether it was hidden
c9 to c12 at UAA, 119 of 150 cited used AI, about 1.1% of 10,500+ students, 73% and 56% rises with no stated baseline (UAA only)
c8 and c21 until now rules were set class by class and UAF had no unified policy
c13 AI can recommend, a person decides
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: The rebuttal at full strength (c17 to c19): administrators and board members knew, a person decided, and drafting help is not a student passing off AI work. A label puts the human decision on the record rather than leaving it to who was in which meeting.
angle.falsifiability: False if the public draft carried an AI-use note before October 9th, or if either side denied AI was used.
honesty_constraints: Claude-drafted claim attributed to Hartley and Potter as opinion
Misconduct figures UAA only, say cited for misconduct
Disclose the pipeline itself is built on Claude
angle.cross_challenge: Analyst 3 warned 1.1% is a floor not a verdict (cited cases are only the caught ones), so the film never says 1.1% used AI improperly. Analyst 2's constructive lens was kept but not allowed to claim adoption. Analyst 1's thesis was kept because it is the only one with a falsifiable observation and a drawable object.
